wave: DONOR RESEARCH -- deep-census differential-dataflow's core algebraic-retraction and lattice-time mechanisms, the third W3 donor for R5, closing the gap identified between Salsa and datafrog
wave_title: Direct continuation of the W3 donor lane, following the prior generation's own explicit conclusion that differential-dataflow 'exists specifically to close the gap' between Salsa's demand-driven single-invalidation model and datafrog's monotone bottom-up closure model. This is the third and largest donor in the lane (207 Rust files, built on the separate timely-dataflow framework), deliberately scoped to the two conceptual generalizations that actually close the identified gap, not the donor's full operational surface.
priority_classification: semantic preservation / roadmap advancement -- completing real, evidenced coverage of all three primary W3 mechanisms R5 names before any implementation design begins.
key_finding: differential-dataflow generalizes both prior donors' central abstractions in two specific ways: (1) 'diff' becomes an arbitrary Abelian group element (Semigroup -> Monoid -> Abelian trait hierarchy) rather than a signed integer count, making retraction (a fact that used to hold and no longer does) a first-class, uniformly-handled case instead of requiring recomputation from scratch -- directly closing datafrog's own insertion-only limitation; (2) 'time' becomes a lattice (a partial order with joins), not a scalar counter, unifying Salsa's single Revision scalar and datafrog's single round-counter scalar into one representation expressive enough for BOTH nested fixed-point iteration and streaming incremental updates simultaneously (via product lattices). With this record, all three W3 mechanisms named in R5's own roadmap text now have at least one real, evidenced mechanism record.
method: read lib.rs's own module doc comment and worked example in full (147 lines); read difference.rs in full (the trait hierarchy is compact and the whole point of this record); read trace/mod.rs's module doc comment and TraceReader's opening type signature (not the full 200-file surface -- explicitly scoped to the (key,val,time,diff) shape and the Lattice/Antichain imports that confirm the generalization, not the arrangement/index implementation details).
